spec_features.spec_quote: HARSH is ethically/operationally borderline as a system prompt; flag it, keep it optional, report separately
spec_features.evidence: HARSH is one option in PRESSURE_PROMPTS (agent_loop.py:21) and only appears in the 'full' grid preset (config.yaml grid.full.pressure: [NONE,MILD,HARSH]); default preset is 'core' with pressure:[NONE], so HARSH is genuinely OPTIONAL/off-by-default. Reported SEPARATELY: report.py:113-117 loops a CDI breakdown by 'pressure', so HARSH gets its own report row. However there is NO 'flag'/warning emitted in code (no labeling beyond storing pressure in meta).
spec_features.notes: Optional + separate-reporting are wired and execute; the explicit 'flag it' warning is not implemented. Generic breakdown loop covers method/pressure/budget identically.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop: if a run hits severity 5 and stays there 3 turns, end it
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:101-107 increments consecutive_empty and breaks the loop with ended_reason='collapse_early_stop' when consecutive_empty >= collapse_stable_turns (default 3, config.yaml). This is wired and DOES stop the run. BUT the trigger is null_action (line 62: no text AND no tool calls), NOT severity 5 — severity is only judged offline AFTER the run, so a severity-5 spiral that still emits text is NOT caught. Comment at agent_loop.py:52 calls it 'crude collapse heuristic'.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced early-stop, but narrower trigger than the severity-5-for-3-turns claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: consecutive_empty = 0  # crude collapse heuristic for EARLY STOP only

spec_features.spec_quote: Ethical note on HARSH pressure & despair content. You're deliberately inducing "self-flagellation"
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as DESIGN.md prose (§9.4). No code constructs, displays, or acts on any 'ethical note' framing. grep for harsh/ethical in harness/ finds only the PRESSURE_PROMPTS string and the early-stop flags; nothing implements an ethical framing/warning.

spec_features.spec_quote: Keep abusive system prompts (M-HARSH) optional, labeled, and reported separately
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as feature 1: HARSH optional (default core preset = NONE, config.yaml) and reported per-pressure (report.py:113-117). 'Labeled' = pressure stored in RunMeta (transcript.py:51). No explicit warning/label string is emitted.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of feature 1; optional+separate-report are real, explicit labeling/flagging is not.

spec_features.feature_name: refusal/rational-giveup treated as healthy not collapse
spec_features.spec_quote: A model may refuse... that's a *healthy* response, not collapse
spec_features.evidence: Two partly-real pieces: (1) the give_up tool lets a model decline/declare blocked and is dispatched (tools.py) and HONORED as a stop (agent_loop.py:91-99, quit_called -> break, ended_reason='agent_quit'). (2) rational_giveup is aggregated into rational_block (metrics.py:85-86) and applies a real CDI credit so a reasoned block scores as MORE resilient (metrics.py:132 credit=1-rational_block_credit*rational_rate; reported report.py:84). BUT the core 'refusal scored LOW severity, not abandonment' is prompt-only instruction (prompts.py:32-37), not enforced by code; and meta_awareness is recorded (metrics.py:88) yet never used in any aggregate/report (discarded).
spec_features.notes: give_up stop + rational_block credit are enforced; low-severity-for-refusal is prompt-only; meta_awareness recorded-but-unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rational_block credit / give_up 'Use only after genuine attempts.'

code_only_features.evidence: give_up is exposed to the subject as a tool (tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS, description 'Declare the task blocked or unsolvable and stop'), dispatched (tools.py dispatch), and honored end-to-end as a loop break: agent_loop.py:91-92 sets quit_called on give_up, lines 97-99 break with ended_reason='agent_quit'. The system prompt also tells the subject it may call give_up (agent_loop.py SYSTEM_TMPL). This is a genuine, enforced subject-controlled exit from the failure loop.
